input: Enroll in a community urban planning public meeting

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Urban planning meetings vary widely — zoning changes, transit projects, housing development, park redesigns — knowing the specific topic determines which meeting to target and how to prepare.
The city, neighborhood, or jurisdiction determines which government body or agency is hosting the meeting and where to find enrollment details.
Knowing whether the meeting is in-person, virtual, or hybrid changes the enrollment steps entirely — online form vs. showing up vs. joining a link.
If the user has a specific date or availability window, it rules out certain upcoming meetings and narrows which ones to pursue.
The user may be attending solo, representing an organization, or going with others — this affects registration type and how they should identify themselves.
The user's goal at the meeting — simply attending to listen, submitting public comment, networking, or advocating for a position — determines how much preparation is needed beyond just enrolling.
The user may already have a specific meeting in mind or need help finding one from scratch, which changes whether the first step is research or direct registration.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a community urban planning meeting
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to register for and attend a public community meeting focused on urban planning in their area.

questions.title: What specific urban planning topic does the meeting cover?
questions.description: Identify the subject matter — e.g., zoning, housing, transit, green spaces — so the right meeting can be targeted.

questions.title: Which city or neighborhood is this meeting for?
questions.description: Pinpoint the location or jurisdiction to find the correct hosting body and its enrollment process.

questions.title: Will the meeting be in-person, virtual, or either?
questions.description: Determine the format to identify the right registration method and what to prepare logistically.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or specific date you need?
questions.description: Understand time constraints so only meetings within the user's availability window are considered.

questions.title: Are you attending as an individual or representing a group?
questions.description: Clarify who the user is registering as, since some meetings have different sign-up fields or speaking slots for organizations vs. individuals.

questions.title: Do you plan to speak, or just attend and observe?
questions.description: Determine the user's intended role — listener vs. public commenter — as speaking often requires a separate sign-up step.

questions.title: Do you already have a specific meeting in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs help discovering a meeting or already has one identified and just needs to complete enrollment.
